If all candidates fail, it explicitly returns report=None (not an empty string), established='' and proof_body=''. outcomes.score records format_valid as report is not None, so the failure remains visible as an invalid answer. A valid later candidate is the requested submission. Preserve this deliberately exposed grader source verbatim because it is part of the model prompt.

A child can exit between group lookup and kill. ProcessLookupError means the target group is already gone, satisfying termination; every other OS error propagates.

A TimeoutExpired is handled explicitly rather than reported as success. For the handler whose body returns a result dictionary, that dictionary directly marks timed_out=True and exit_code=None. For the handler whose body calls os.waitpid, this is cleanup after SIGKILL and a bounded Popen.wait; waitpid directly reaps that child when Popen's internal wait lock times out. Each handler's own body provides the distinct timeout handling; neither creates a successful stage result.

This exact waitpid uses process.pid from the Popen child just sent SIGKILL, with options=0. ChildProcessError is Python's ECHILD: this PID has no waitable child status for this parent, for example because Popen or another reaper already consumed it. No live waitable child is skipped by handling ECHILD; that is precisely the reaping postcondition. Other OSError values propagate. The original stage outcome is not changed by this cleanup handler, and stage timeouts remain timed_out=True with exit_code=None.
EOF from the analysis child is converted to an explicit ended message; the parent then raises a RuntimeError for analysis ending without a result. This never creates a valid analysis.
TimeCap is converted to an explicit time-cap finish reason in persisted pilot state; it stops further stages and does not report a successful analysis.
Atomic replacement has already moved the temporary file on success. Cleanup ignores only FileNotFoundError for that now-absent temporary path; write, fsync and replace failures propagate.

The timeout handler immediately returns an explicit failure record with ok=False, axioms=None and why=timeout. It does not continue into the successful subprocess-output path or invent a proof result. This justification is limited to the visible function's failure reporting.
Malformed Lean output is returned with an explicit unexpected-output diagnostic in INCONCLUSIVE. It is not treated as a proved or disproved proposition.

Cleanup deliberately keeps running after failures so results can be copied and pod removal attempted. It preserves the remote code and marks copy/removal failures nonzero before returning; disabling errexit cannot turn those failures into success.

REMOTE_JOB_OUT is an optional test-isolation override. The production driver intentionally leaves it unset and accesses the runner's fixed out/ directory relative to HOME, including out/LAUNCH_ID and out/EXIT_CODE. Thus omission is the standard production interface, not a missing required setting. The next line explicitly logs the selected path and override name. A nonempty supplied path is used exactly; mkdir failure exits 3 rather than selecting a different directory.

text: GRACE=${AUTOSTOP_GRACE_SECONDS:-600}  # time for the driver to copy results before the pod is removed
reason: AUTOSTOP_GRACE_SECONDS is an optional duration override; 600 seconds is the standard result-copy window. The runner prints the selected grace period and the override name immediately, validates it as a whole number before job launch and includes it in the removal deadline. This is an observable configuration choice, not substituted measurements or error results.

REMOTE_JOB_PIDS is an optional test-isolation override, not a required production configuration variable. The production driver does not set it: all launches deliberately share $HOME/.remote_job.pids so stop_previous can find and stop the predecessor session. The next line prints the selected state-file path and override name. Tests set distinct paths for independent fake pods. A supplied nonempty path is used exactly; a read/write failure does not select another path. This default therefore implements the normal production interface visibly rather than hiding a missing required setting.
